nodes.description:
Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, with or without beta blockers, are the first-line treatment for the dilated cardiomyopathy - which matters because the cardiomyopathy is what kills in this disease.
The Becker-specific point is where the indication stops. In Duchenne, prophylactic ACE inhibition is given regardless of ejection fraction; in Becker it is not, because no trial has tested it in patients with a normal LVEF. The French guidelines say plainly that there is no indication to treat every Becker patient regardless of cardiac phenotype the way one would in Duchenne. Treatment is instead triggered by LVEF below 50% or myocardial fibrosis on MRI, and considered case by case in that group.
Reading this as "ACE inhibitors are used in BMD" and stopping there would import a Duchenne practice into a disease where it has never been tested.

nodes.description: Dystrophin mechanically couples the actin cytoskeleton to the extracellular matrix through the sarcolemma; without it, contraction tears the membrane. A semifunctional internally deleted dystrophin still performs some of that coupling, so injury per contraction is reduced rather than abolished, and muscle is lost slowly instead of rapidly.

evidence.snippet: Becker muscular dystrophy (BMD) is an X-linked neuromuscular disease attributable to mutations in DMD, leading to a deficient and less functional dystrophin, mainly in skeletal and cardiac muscle.

nodes.description: The defining lesion class. In the largest Becker cohort assembled, 86% of patients carried in-frame deletions or duplications of DMD. Deletions clustering around exons 45-55 dominate, and the specific deletion carries prognostic information: within the same in-frame class, del45-49 is associated with earlier loss of ambulation than del45-47, while del45-55, del48 and del48-49 are associated with later loss of ambulation. So "in-frame" sets the disease and the particular exons set the severity.

nodes.description:
The rate-limiting state of the whole entry, and the single node on which the Becker/Duchenne distinction rests. A shorter, lower-molecular-weight dystrophin is produced and it is semifunctional - not normal, not absent.
This is why the disease is a spectrum rather than a category. Duchenne has essentially no functional protein and a stereotyped course; Becker has a variable amount of partly working protein, and the residual function tracks which internal domains the deletion removed. The entry therefore does not curate a single severity, and the natural-history data below are reported as distributions rather than as a description of a typical patient.

nodes.description:
Around 30% of patients have left ventricular impairment, an order of magnitude more than the 2.7% with respiratory involvement. It is also under genotypic control within the in-frame class: del45-55 and del48 are associated with significantly lower odds of a pathological left ventricular ejection fraction than del45-47.
The clinically important consequence is that cardiac surveillance in Becker cannot be triggered by skeletal-muscle severity. A patient walking normally at fifty can have a failing ventricle, and the deletion that predicts a good ambulatory course is not always the one that predicts a good cardiac course.
It is also what kills. Heart failure from dilated cardiomyopathy is the most common cause of death in Becker muscular dystrophy, with a mean age of death in the mid-forties - against a median age at loss of ambulation estimated at sixty-nine. Those two numbers together are the whole prognostic shape of this disease: most patients are still walking when the heart fails, so an entry that read only the skeletal-muscle data would describe an indolent condition and be wrong about its outcome.

nodes.description:
The skeletal-muscle endpoint, and it is strikingly indolent. In a 943-patient cohort followed at 17 centres, only 13.5% had lost ambulation by last assessment, with a Kaplan-Meier median age at loss of ambulation estimated at 69 years. Diagnosis is frequently incidental: 55% were prompted by a chance finding of raised creatine kinase, at a median age of 7.5 years - decades before weakness would have brought them in.
Respiratory involvement is uncommon and mild, but not absent, and its rate changes with ambulatory status: forced vital capacity falls about 1% of predicted per year overall, and significantly faster after loss of ambulation. That is the argument for following respiratory function in the non-ambulant subgroup specifically rather than in everyone equally.
